hyps.why: With edge 5 removed, the direct edge carries more of the output signal, so improving it matters more.
Without the direct edge, edge 5 is a main route to the output, so a better op there matters more.
Edge 1 reaches the output only through edge 5, so the conv is wasted if edge 5 is removed.
Edge 4 starts at node 1, which is unreachable when edge 0 is removed.
With edge 4 removed, edge 0 is the only way into the longer route to the output, so improving it matters more.
Removing edge 0 when edge 1 is already removed disconnects nodes 1 and 2, leaving only the direct edge.
Removing edge 1 when edge 0 is already removed disconnects nodes 1 and 2, leaving only the direct edge.
A skip on the direct edge already supplies a clean path to the output, so a conv on edge 5 adds less.
Pooling on an empty direct edge adds a path to the output, whereas it replaces a better op elsewhere.
Adding a residual shortcut from input to output where none existed helps accuracy, unlike replacing a conv with a skip.
